questions.q: Which two record types together define a Scripted REST API?
options: A Script Include and a UI Action
A single sys_ws_definition record that holds everything, with no child records
A Business Rule and a Client Script
sys_ws_definition (the API and its base path) and a Resource record (the method, relative path, and script) under it
questions.explain: sys_ws_definition defines the API and its shared base path; each Resource child record adds one endpoint with its own path, method, and script.

questions.q: In a Scripted REST Resource script, which object do you use to send JSON data back to the caller?
options: response, via response.setBody()
gs, via gs.setBody()
current, via current.setBody()
request, via request.setBody()
questions.explain: response.setBody() serializes a JavaScript object as the JSON response; response.setStatus() sets the HTTP status code.

options: The sys_id of the Incident record
Nothing — pathParams only works with query strings, not {placeholder} segments
The string "INC0010023", parsed automatically from the {number} placeholder in the URL path
The entire request body as a JSON object
questions.explain: A {placeholder} segment in a Resource's relative path is parsed automatically into request.pathParams under that same key name.

options: The response is sent with HTTP status 404 and a JSON body containing an error message
An empty 200 OK response is sent with no body
The script throws an uncaught exception and the server crashes
ServiceNow automatically retries the GlideRecord query
questions.explain: gr.next() returns false when the query found no matching record, so the script explicitly sets a 404 status and an error payload before returning.

questions.q: Why would a Resource use request.queryParams instead of a {placeholder} path parameter?
options: There's no real difference — they're interchangeable in every case
queryParams is required for every Scripted REST Resource regardless of design
Query parameters suit filtering or optional values on top of a request, rather than identifying which specific resource is being requested
Path parameters can only be used with POST requests
questions.explain: Path parameters identify which resource you mean (one specific incident); query parameters typically add filters or options on top of that.
